notes: §1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR3 has two sentences: GENERATE, INITIATE or TERMINATE 'must not appear in a paragraph within a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure', and 'A PERFORM statement in a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure must not have GENERATE, INITIATE, or TERMINATE statements in its range.' The first is ReportWriterBinder#RejectInBeforeReporting over EnclosingContext#InBeforeReportingProcedure, read by BindGenerate/BindInitiate/BindTerminate at every edition (COBOL2378). The second is VersionConformancePass#GateBeforeReportingPerformRange at --std 85 (COBOL7234, kb/Work PB5254): each out-of-line PERFORM written in a USE BEFORE REPORTING section is asked the static range ProcedureReach.Closure models (§1985:VI.6.21.4 GR11: the performed paragraphs and every procedure they PERFORM, transitively; a GO TO is a run-time fact and is not followed), and a GENERATE, INITIATE or TERMINATE there is reported at the PERFORM. 2002 and later replace the sentence by the run-time EC-FLOW-REPORT of §2023:14.9.49.4 GR10 (kb/Work PB326), so the program compiles there.

next.reason: 1985: "A PERFORM statement in a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure must not have GENERATE, INITIATE, or TERMINATE statements in its range."; 2023: "If a GENERATE, INITIATE, or TERMINATE statement is executed within the range of a declarative ... EC-FLOW-REPORT ... is set". The paragraph ban is kept verbatim. The PERFORM-range ban is no longer a syntax rule: execution in the range is defined as unsuccessful and sets EC-FLOW-REPORT.
